bullets: [1] Define any linear equation of one variable (e.g. y = 3x+2)
[2] Select 5 different values for x (x1, x2,… x10) and calculate corresponding y values
[3] Use x and y values as training data , apply MSSE technique to obtain the equation of the line that best fit on the training data (compare to your defined equation)
[4] Repeat 1,2, and 3 after adding random noise term to the equation (e.g. y = 3x+2 + random(0..1)

recreation_brief: 1. Set slide background to light gray (#F2F2F2) and draw a thin dark-red border rectangle around the entire slide edge. 2. Add a yellow circle (#FFFF99) with black text '36' at the top-right corner. 3. Place centered bold title near top: 'Assignment #2: ' in red (#C00000) followed by 'Part 1 - Prediction' in blue (#0000CC). 4. Draw a white rectangle with thin blue border spanning ~80% width below the title; inside it add four lines of black text: '[1] Define any linear equation of one variable (e.g. y = 3x+2)', '[2] Select 5 different values for x (x1, x2,… x10) and calculate corresponding y values' (with the standalone x and y colored red), '[3] Use x and y values as training data , apply MSSE technique to obtain the equation of the line that best fit on the training data (compare to your defined equation)', '[4] Repeat 1,2, and 3 after adding random noise term to the equation (e.g. y = 3x+2 + random(0..1)'. 5. Bottom-left: draw a white square with red border; inside draw red L-shaped axes, label vertical axis 'y' in red at top and horizontal axis 'x' in red at right; plot 5 steel-blue (#5B7FA6) dots ascending linearly from lower-left to upper-right. 6. Bottom-right: duplicate the same plot style with 5 blue dots ascending but with slightly more vertical scatter (noise). 7. Ensure no axis ticks, gridlines, or trend lines are drawn on either plot.
